task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the freelancers behind Foldstage Crew and the business of making temporary venues work for an evening.

facts.text: A July 2026 work note records Foldstage Crew labeling dismantled ticket-booth panels after the audience had left a community concert.
Foldstage is a shared booking desk for 11 freelance event workers, not a company employing all members on fixed weekly schedules.
Members handle ticket booths, barriers, signs and small-event front-of-house layouts; specialist rigging is contracted separately.
The quoted labor rate is $180 per worker for up to eight agreed working hours; extra time is billed under the individual booking's terms.
The group does not publish one universal rate for transport, accommodation or specialist equipment.
Organizers often see only public opening hours, while crew bookings also cover delivery, setup, checks and removal.
The shared desk completed five bookings in June and lost a sixth when its organizer canceled before setup.
The canceled booking paid a deposit that covered reserved vehicle costs but did not replace all expected crew income.
Booking coordinator Neri Valen says individual cancellation terms depend on when resources and workers were committed.
Valen said, "An empty square can mean nobody came, or it can mean the crew has already put the whole venue back in the van."
Worker Ceri Dorne combines Foldstage bookings with part-time employment at a furniture warehouse.
Dorne says a late change to an event's finishing time can conflict with the next morning's separate job.
Dorne said, "The audience buys an evening. I have to fit that evening between two other working days."
The booking desk keeps a shared availability calendar but cannot guarantee members a minimum number of paid days.
Its reusable booth panels are owned by three members and hired to bookings through a separate equipment charge.
The equipment charge is not automatically divided as wages among every person on the crew.
A community organizer says knowing the full setup and removal cost helps compare using an existing hall with building a temporary venue.
The record contains no complete profit account or evidence that every temporary event is cheaper than a permanent venue.
Foldstage stores signs and booth panels in a former coach garage with painted outlines showing where components belong.
The group has discussed a larger shared store but has neither signed a lease nor agreed how its cost would be divided.

forbidden_additions: All members have guaranteed company wages or deposits replace every canceled day's income
One all-inclusive universal fee, specialist rigging by this crew or a signed new store lease
